patches.old: A critical concept: antidepressants take *2–4 weeks* to produce clinical improvement despite producing immediate neurochemical changes. This lag is thought to reflect downstream receptor desensitization and neuroplastic changes, including increased **BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor)** expression and hippocampal neurogenesis.
patches.new: A critical concept: antidepressants block reuptake within hours but take weeks to produce clinical improvement — partial response is often visible by 2 weeks, with full response typically requiring **4–6 weeks**. The leading explanation is the **autoreceptor account**. Blocking SERT raises serotonin not only at the terminal but also around the cell bodies in the raphe nuclei, where **somatodendritic 5-HT1A autoreceptors** detect the rise and cut the neuron's firing rate, so little extra serotonin actually reaches forebrain targets at first. Over the following weeks those autoreceptors **desensitize**, firing recovers while the reuptake blockade remains in place, and synaptic serotonin finally rises downstream. Slower changes follow and are thought to consolidate the response: postsynaptic receptor adaptation, increased **BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor)** expression, and hippocampal neurogenesis. This is why a trial is not judged a failure at two weeks.

patches.old: **Deep brain stimulation (DBS)** involves surgically implanting electrodes to modulate specific circuits (e.g., subgenual cingulate cortex for depression, subthalamic nucleus for OCD).
patches.new: **Deep brain stimulation (DBS)** involves surgically implanting electrodes to modulate specific circuits — the subgenual cingulate cortex for depression, and for treatment-refractory OCD the **anterior limb of the internal capsule and the adjacent ventral striatum**, which is the target the FDA approved under a humanitarian device exemption in 2009. The subthalamic nucleus, the familiar target in Parkinson's disease, has also been trialled for OCD but is not the approved site.

sources.title: Pinckard-Dover, Ward & Foote, Frontiers in Surgery (2021) — records the February 2009 FDA humanitarian device exemption for deep brain stimulation of the anterior limb of the internal capsule in refractory OCD

visual.title: The lag, the classes, and the three levels
visual.alt: Three stages of the antidepressant delay: on day one SERT blockade raises serotonin but autoreceptors cut firing; over weeks one to three those autoreceptors desensitize and firing recovers on top of the blockade; by weeks four to six postsynaptic adaptation, BDNF and neurogenesis consolidate the response. Alongside, a table of drug classes with mechanism, indication and signature adverse effect, and a panel of the biological, psychological and sociocultural levels with the barrier typical of each.
visual.caption: The chemistry is immediate; the clinical effect is not. The gap is the autoreceptor brake, and it takes weeks to wear off.
